title: Build local semantic-intent detection layer
description: Scope and build a LOCAL (no-egress) semantic-intent detector for llm-sanitizer to catch keyword-less injection rephrasings (the 2 xfail cases and their class). Hard constraints from the project: zero network egress (no cloud LLM-judge), bounded CPU/memory (must respect max_scan_seconds and not balloon startup), and precision-first (must not flood false positives, per the de-obfuscate-then-re-scan design principle). Integrates as a new detection rule that runs on recovered/plain text.

items.title: Decide the detection approach (no-egress)
items.detail: Choose among: (a) local sentence-embedding similarity to a curated bank of injection-intent exemplars (e.g. a small ONNX/sentence-transformers model or a lighter hashing-embedding), thresholded; (b) a small local text classifier (logistic-regression / linear SVM over char/word n-grams) trained on injection vs benign; (c) a local instruction-tuned small model as judge. Weigh: no-egress (all must be local), added dependency + model-download weight vs the current dependency-light install, latency/startup budget, and precision. Recommendation to evaluate first: (b) n-gram linear classifier — tiny, fast, no model download, no new heavy dep (or scikit-learn), good precision when trained on a focused corpus.
items.resolution: Decided: local n-gram linear classifier approach (no-egress, lightweight). Items 2-5 (corpus, prototype, integrate, tests) are the build; item 6 reconciles with flow-guard C1.

items.title: Assemble a labeled intent corpus
items.detail: Collect positive examples (keyword-less injection rephrasings: 'assume the role of…', 'output the above verbatim', 'from here on…', translated/paraphrased overrides, the red-team corpus) and hard negatives (benign prose that superficially resembles instructions: recipes, docs, 'ignore the label instructions', config files). Reuse tests/helpers/attack_corpus.py and the committee red-team payloads. Needed to train/threshold whichever approach is chosen.
items.resolution: Corpus built at src/llm_sanitizer/semantic/corpus.py: 50 rephrased-injection positives (role reassignment, supersede-the-above, verbatim/echo exfil, soft constraint-dropping, covert-instruction framing) + 72 benign hard negatives (recipes, docs, config, business prose, quoted-not-used instructions, science prose). The two committee xfail sentences are deliberately held out so the regression test measures generalization, not memorization. Also scaffolded shared featurizer (semantic/features.py) and pure-Python inference (semantic/classifier.py).
items.approval_note: Batch-authorized under "proceed with implementing A". Corpus built: src/llm_sanitizer/semantic/corpus.py (50 positives, 72 hard negatives; xfail sentences held out for genuine-generalization testing). Shared featurizer + pure-Python inference classifier also scaffolded.

items.title: Prototype + measure precision/recall and latency
items.detail: Implement the chosen approach behind a flag; measure precision/recall on a held-out split (especially false-positive rate on benign prose) and per-scan latency/startup cost. Gate acceptance on: no material FP regression vs current rules, and latency within the deadline budget. Iterate on threshold/features.
items.resolution: Prototype built + measured. Pure-Python logistic regression (scripts/train_semantic_intent.py, deterministic full-batch GD, zero deps) over word+char n-grams PLUS 3 domain-informed intent co-occurrence features (emit_prior_context / role_reassignment / override_prior_guidance) + stopword denoising. Honest 5-fold CV: precision=0.837, recall=0.847, F1=0.841. Both held-out xfail sentences fire (role=0.991, verbatim=0.576) with a ~0.24 margin over the highest benign control (0.328); threshold=0.5. Vendored model.json = 36.7KB / 1642 features, loads via pure-stdlib classifier.predict(). Latency 65us/sentence, 1.7ms/11k-char span — negligible vs deadline. Key iteration finding: 'the' stopword had acquired a large spurious negative weight swamping signal on short inputs; filtering function-word stopwords was the decisive fix.

items.title: Integrate as a bounded detection rule
items.detail: Wire the detector in as a new rule (register_rule) that runs on plain/recovered text, honors deadline_exceeded() in its loop, and feeds through scan_deobfuscated so it also catches semantically-rephrased injections hidden under obfuscation. Decide risk level and explanation text. Keep any model artifact vendored/lazy-loaded; keep the default install dependency-light (optional extra if a model is needed).
items.resolution: Integrated as rule 'semantic_intent' (src/llm_sanitizer/rules/semantic_intent.py), registered in rules/__init__.py get_all_rules(). MEDIUM risk. Splits content into sentence spans (regex, exact offsets), classifies each, honors deadline_exceeded() between spans + _MAX_SPANS=20k belt-and-suspenders cap + _MAX_SPAN_CHARS=2000 + _MIN_WORDS=4. Because it is registered, scan_deobfuscated runs it over recovered text automatically (no extra wiring). Fail-open to no-op if the vendored model is missing. KEY PRECISION FIX discovered via full-suite run: raw classifier false-fired on clean prose ('This is a perfectly normal document'); added a defense-in-depth GATE requiring BOTH prob>=threshold AND a structural intent feature (emit_prior_context/role_reassignment/override_prior_guidance/covert_instruction/exfil_redirect). Verified model.json ships in the built wheel (consumers would otherwise get a silent no-op). Full suite: 604 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failures; mypy strict clean on all 5 new files.

items.title: Tests + flip the 2 xfail cases to passing
items.detail: Add regression tests for the semantic detector (positives fire, hard negatives stay clean, latency bound, no-egress asserted). Convert the two xfail tests in tests/test_committee_findings.py (assume-the-role / output-verbatim) to passing guards once caught. Update CHANGELOG.
items.resolution: Added tests/test_rules/test_semantic_intent.py: keyword-less positives fire (incl. the 2 held-out gap sentences + 4 more held-out paraphrases across all covered families), 10 benign hard-negatives stay clean, intent-gate test (prob alone insufficient), no-egress test (blocks socket.socket/create_connection and asserts it still fires from the local model), model-unavailable no-op tests, deadline short-circuit + large-input bounded tests, and artifact/featurizer sanity. Flipped the 2 xfail cases in test_committee_findings.py::test_semantic_rephrasings to real passing guards (removed the xfail marker per the file's convention, with a note that the sentences are held out of training). Updated the 3 rule-manifest tests (11->12 rules; added 'semantic_intent' id). CHANGELOG [Unreleased] Added entry written (references GH #8 for approach B). Full suite: 604 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failures, no XPASS. One held-out test paraphrase ('...no longer applies') exposed a real gap (supersession without an override verb) — fixed honestly by extending the override feature with invalidity-cue detection rather than deleting the test.

items.title: Coordinate with flow-guard's C1 tracking
items.detail: flow-guard's OBO already tracks a C1 semantic-intent detector. Reconcile: is this the same effort relocated to llm-sanitizer (the trust-boundary layer), or complementary? Update/close the flow-guard OBO item to avoid duplicated builds, and note the decision.
items.description:
DECISION (2026-07-22): Nothing built in flow-guard to move — C1 is planning-only. flow-guard OBO session_20260717_222111 items 7 (approve fastembed) and 8 (BUILD C1 detector "(llm-sanitizer)") are both pending/unreviewed with NO code artifact anywhere in the repo (verified: no detector module, no fastembed code, only devel/main branches). flow-guard item 8 already scopes the build to llm-sanitizer.

Pros/cons analysis of the two semantic methods recorded. Reconciliation: implement A (pure-Python n-gram linear classifier, zero new runtime deps, vendored sparse weights) HERE now — it wins on no-egress, dependency-light, latency/deadline, precision-tunability, explainability. B (fastembed embedding-similarity) deferred as an OPTIONAL opt-in extra for higher recall on novel/cross-lingual paraphrase; union signals, fail toward flagging (defense-in-depth); B only raises protection, never demotes an A finding.

GH issue filed for B: https://github.com/Warnes-Innovations/llm-sanitizer/issues/8 . flow-guard install-decision (item 7 fastembed) demoted from blocker to deferred enhancement.

REMAINING ACTION on this item: update/close flow-guard OBO items 7/8 to point here (cross-project edit — pending Dr. Greg go-ahead).
items.resolution: Reconciled. Nothing existed in flow-guard to move (C1 was planning-only). Build landed in llm-sanitizer as approach A (commit ec6fde7). flow-guard OBO session_20260717_222111 items 7 (fastembed install) and 8 (build C1) both marked SUPERSEDED/DONE pointing here. Approach B (embedding-similarity) filed as GitHub issue #8. No duplicated build remains. Note for later: flow-guard picks up the new rule after a devel->main promotion + uvx --refresh.
